Subject: DPA: cross-border clauses + dataflow clarifications

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for moving quickly on the DPA. Before we take your redlines into legal, we want to clarify a few cross-border/dataflow items your team flagged so we can propose a single consolidated response. Attached: rdw-dataflow-v2.pdf (annotated dataflow) and our initial dpa-proposed-redlines.docx.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Export controls/EEA-to-non-EEA: you referenced additional export-control language for regulated healthcare customers — can you confirm the exact triggering conditions (specific product lines or customer data classes)?
- KMS/key custody: which option is preferred: (A) customer-managed CMEK in AcmeCloud EU region (customer holds keys), (B) Redwood-managed keys with EU-only residency and customer key-wrapping, or (C) hybrid (Redwood wraps with customer KEK)? We can support all three but need to know what AcmeCloud requires for the procurement docs.
- Subprocessor scope: your list indicated a new analytics subprocessor in APAC. Please confirm whether that subprocessor will ever receive token-level identifiers or only aggregated telemetry.
- Retention & localization: for exported artifacts (logs/telemetry), can AcmeCloud accept pseudonymized telemetry stored outside EU if the PII payloads remain in-region?

We'd like to propose a 30-minute call next week to go over these items and capture any small DPA language changes live (saves repeated redlines). If helpful, we can draft a narrow export-control clause to propose to your legal team.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA: cross-border clauses + dataflow clarifications

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 

- Export controls/triggering conditions: this is product-specific — our healthcare customers (PHI) and anything marked as "sensitive personal data" in our classification matrix require explicit export-control language. In practice that means any export of raw PII or unredacted transcripts. Aggregated telemetry is fine.

- KMS/key custody: AcmeCloud's preference is (A) customer-managed CMEK for production keys. For short-term evaluational dev/test we accept Redwood-managed keys with contractual guarantees and EU residency, but procurement will push for CMEK in the EU for production.

- Subprocessor scope: the APAC analytics vendor (AnalyticsCo APAC) will only receive aggregated telemetry and metrics; they will not receive token-level IDs or raw transcripts. We'll attach the official subprocessor roster (sending now).

- Retention & localization: we can accept pseudonymized telemetry outside the EEA provided the pseudonymization is non-reversible and the mapping is kept in-region under AcmeCloud control.

I'm attaching our current subprocessor export (acme_subprocessors_20280621.csv). Our legal ops would like Redwood to propose the narrow export-control clause you mentioned; please share a suggested clause and we'll run it through legal.

Happy to meet — legal suggests Fri 2028-07-01 10:00 CEST. Proposal: Kimberly + Marissa + Jonas + Hannah + Sanjay + Legal Ops.

Best regards,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Platform Security & Compliance
AcmeCloud

Sanjay / team —

Thanks for the fast answers and the subprocessor export. Two operational follow-ups from engineering/ops perspective: 

1) KMS implementation options we can support:
   - Option A (preferred for AcmeCloud production): Customer-managed CMEK (we require a short onboarding checklist and a policy doc to confirm rotation/backup).
   - Option B: Redwood-managed keys with EU residency + HSM-backed KEK; Redwood provides KMS attestation & monthly key-rotation evidence.
   - Option C: Customer-supplied KEK for envelope-wrapping (hybrid).

2) Telemetry & pseudonymization: our recommendation is to keep the mapping table (token->PII) in AcmeCloud-managed storage (EU region). Redwood will only store one-way pseudonyms and aggregated metrics. Where customers need on-prem or VPC-only telemetry exports we can route via our Dedicated offering.

I've attached a proposed subproc mapping that marks which subprocessors will see token-level telemetry vs aggregated (subproc-mapping-proposal.xlsx). Please confirm AnalyticsCo APAC is marked as aggregated-only.

Finally, we can draft the export-control clause. Jonas, could you propose a tight clause text we can send to Sanjay/legal?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: DPA: cross-border clauses + dataflow clarifications

Marissa / Sanjay —

Quick technical read of Kimberly's diagram: the annotated flow looks like (high level)
- Ingest (AcmeCloud region) -> transient KV/prefix cache (Redwood edge) -> model runtime (EU GPUs) -> output returned to AcmeCloud endpoint.

Operational notes: we can ensure that raw transcripts and PII fields never leave the AcmeCloud region by performing prefix/KV caching stripping before export and using in-region preprocessing. For the pseudonymization spec: we suggest using a one-way HMAC with per-customer salt (stored in-customer) + per-request nonce; that avoids reversible token maps on Redwood side.

Proposed narrow export-control clause (suggested redline to DPA):
"Export Controls and Cross-Border Processing: Where Customer Data is classified by Customer as 'Sensitive Personal Data' (including PHI or other regulated health data), Processor shall not transfer raw or unredacted Customer Data outside the EEA without Customer's prior written consent. Processor may transfer pseudonymized telemetry and aggregated analytics provided (a) pseudonymization is performed by an irreversible cryptographic transform and (b) any mapping key or salt enabling re-identification is retained exclusively by Customer in the EEA. Processor will implement technical controls (prefix/KV cache stripping, in-region preprocessing) to prevent inadvertent export of Sensitive Personal Data."
If that looks acceptable to AcmeCloud legal, we can fold into the DPA redline doc and run through DocuSign.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Applied Privacy Engineer — Redwood Inference
